subject: Physics
prompt: Speed of a transverse wave on a string under tension T, mass/length μ?
explain: Wave speed on string depends on restoring force (T) and inertia (μ).

subject: Physics
prompt: Speed of sound in an ideal gas is proportional to which power of absolute temp T?
explain: v = √(γRT/M), so v ∝ √T.

subject: Physics
prompt: For a standing wave on a string fixed at both ends, allowed wavelengths (L = length)?
explain: Both ends are nodes; condition gives λₙ = 2L/n, n = 1,2,3…

subject: Physics
prompt: Fundamental frequency of a string of length L, tension T, linear density μ?
explain: First harmonic has one antinode; f₁ = v/2L where v = √(T/μ).

subject: Physics
prompt: For an open pipe of length L, fundamental frequency is?
explain: Open pipe has antinodes at both ends; smallest resonant length = λ/2.

subject: Physics
prompt: For a closed pipe (one end closed), fundamental frequency is?
explain: Closed end = node, open end = antinode; L = λ/4 for fundamental.

subject: Physics
prompt: A closed pipe supports only which harmonics?
explain: Closed pipe: fn = (2n-1)v/4L, so only odd multiples of fundamental.

subject: Physics
prompt: Beats frequency between two sources of frequencies f₁ and f₂ (f₁ > f₂)?
explain: Beats arise from periodic constructive/destructive interference; rate = |f₁−f₂|.

subject: Physics
prompt: Doppler effect: source moves toward stationary observer (v_s = source speed)?
explain: Source approaching compresses wavefronts; denominator decreases → higher freq.

subject: Physics
prompt: Doppler effect: observer moves toward stationary source (v_o = observer speed)?
explain: Observer moving toward source intercepts more wavefronts per second.

subject: Physics
prompt: Relation between wave speed v, frequency f, and wavelength λ?
explain: Fundamental wave relation; holds for all mechanical and EM waves.

subject: Physics
prompt: In a stationary wave, the distance between two consecutive nodes is?
explain: Adjacent nodes are separated by half a wavelength in a standing wave.

subject: Physics
prompt: Distance between a node and the nearest antinode in a standing wave?
explain: Node and adjacent antinode are quarter-wavelength apart.

subject: Physics
prompt: Newton's formula for speed of sound gives γ = 1 (isothermal). Laplace corrected it to?
explain: Laplace: sound propagation is adiabatic, so v = √(γP/ρ), not √(P/ρ).

subject: Physics
prompt: Intensity I of a wave is proportional to which power of amplitude A?
explain: Energy carried by a wave is proportional to the square of its amplitude.

subject: Physics
prompt: Sound level in decibels when intensity is I and reference I₀?
explain: Decibel scale: β = 10 log₁₀(I/I₀); I₀ = 10⁻¹² W/m².

subject: Physics
prompt: Principle of superposition states that resultant displacement is?
explain: Superposition: net displacement = vector (algebraic for 1-D) sum of each wave.

subject: Physics
prompt: Two waves y₁ = A sin(ωt) and y₂ = A sin(ωt+φ). Resultant amplitude?
explain: Using phasor addition: resultant amplitude = 2A cos(φ/2).

subject: Physics
prompt: For constructive interference, path difference Δ must satisfy?
explain: Path difference = whole number of wavelengths → crests meet → constructive.

subject: Physics
prompt: For destructive interference, path difference Δ must satisfy?
explain: Path difference = odd multiple of λ/2 → crest meets trough → cancellation.

subject: Physics
prompt: End correction for a closed pipe (radius r) makes effective length?
explain: End correction ≈ 0.3d for closed end (one open end); accounts for antinode outside pipe.

subject: Physics
prompt: Speed of longitudinal waves in a solid of Young's modulus Y, density ρ?
explain: Longitudinal wave speed in solids: v = √(Y/ρ), Y = Young's modulus.

subject: Physics
prompt: In a standing wave, which points always have zero displacement?
explain: Nodes are fixed points of zero displacement; antinodes have maximum amplitude.

subject: Physics
prompt: General equation of a harmonic progressive wave moving in +x direction?
explain: Wave travelling in +x: phase decreases with x → y = A sin(ωt − kx).

subject: Physics
prompt: Angular wave number k is related to wavelength λ by?
explain: k = 2π/λ; it represents spatial frequency (rad per metre).

subject: Physics
prompt: Speed of sound in a liquid of bulk modulus B, density ρ?
explain: Bulk modulus is the elastic property for liquids; v = √(B/ρ).

subject: Physics
prompt: Phase difference φ and path difference Δ are related by?
explain: One full wavelength corresponds to 2π phase; φ = (2π/λ)Δ.

subject: Physics
prompt: Laplace correction: speed of sound in gas uses which modulus?
explain: Sound propagation is adiabatic; effective modulus = γP, not P.

subject: Physics
prompt: An open pipe of length L: which harmonics are present?
explain: Open pipe has antinodes at both ends; all integer multiples of fundamental exist.

subject: Physics
prompt: Second overtone of a closed pipe equals which harmonic?
explain: Closed pipe: overtones are 3rd, 5th, 7th… harmonics; 2nd overtone = 5th harmonic.

subject: Physics
prompt: Second overtone frequency of an open pipe of length L?
explain: Open pipe 2nd overtone is 3rd harmonic: f₃ = 3v/2L.

subject: Physics
prompt: For resonance in a closed pipe, successive resonating lengths differ by?
explain: Consecutive resonance lengths in a closed pipe differ by half a wavelength.

subject: Physics
prompt: If string tension is quadrupled, fundamental frequency changes by factor?
explain: f ∝ √T; quadrupling T doubles f.

subject: Physics
prompt: A wave y = A sin(ωt − kx): particle velocity at any point is?
explain: Particle velocity vₚ = ∂y/∂t = −(wave speed)×(∂y/∂x) for +x wave.

subject: Physics
prompt: Power transmitted by a transverse wave on string: P ∝?
explain: Average power P = ½μω²A²v; proportional to ω², A², and wave speed v.

subject: Physics
prompt: Intensity of sound is inversely proportional to which power of distance r?
explain: For a point source radiating uniformly, I = P/4πr²; I ∝ 1/r².

subject: Physics
prompt: The ratio of speed of sound in H₂ to O₂ at same temperature? (γ same)
explain: v ∝ √(γRT/M); M(O₂)/M(H₂)=16, so v(H₂)/v(O₂)=√16=4.

subject: Physics
prompt: Doppler: source moves away from stationary observer at speed vₛ, observed freq?
explain: Source receding: denominator increases → f' < f; f' = fv/(v+vₛ).

subject: Physics
prompt: Doppler: observer moves away from stationary source at speed v_o, observed freq?
explain: Observer receding: fewer wavefronts per second; f' = f(v−v_o)/v.

subject: Physics
prompt: Equation of standing wave formed by superposition of two opposite waves?
explain: Superposing y=A sin(ωt−kx) and y=A sin(ωt+kx) gives 2A sin(kx)cos(ωt).

subject: Physics
prompt: In a standing wave, antinodes occur where amplitude is?
explain: Antinodes are positions of maximum displacement amplitude = 2A.

subject: Physics
prompt: For string fixed at one end, free at other: allowed modes have L = ?
explain: Fixed-free string: node at fixed end, antinode at free end; L=(2n−1)λ/4.

subject: Physics
prompt: Pitch of a sound is determined primarily by its?
explain: Pitch is the subjective perception corresponding to frequency of sound.

subject: Physics
prompt: Loudness of sound is determined primarily by its?
explain: Loudness depends on intensity which depends on amplitude squared.

subject: Physics
prompt: If two sound waves have intensity ratio 100:1, their dB difference is?

subject: Physics
prompt: Quality (timbre) of sound depends on?
explain: Timbre distinguishes sounds of same pitch/loudness via their harmonic content.

subject: Physics
prompt: Velocity of sound is maximum in which medium?
explain: Solids have highest elasticity; v_solid > v_liquid > v_gas.

subject: Physics
prompt: Frequency of beats does NOT depend on?
explain: Beat frequency = |f₁−f₂|; amplitudes affect loudness of beats, not frequency.

subject: Physics
prompt: A string has n loops in resonance. Number of nodes (including endpoints)?
explain: n loops → n antinodes and (n+1) nodes (endpoints are nodes).

subject: Physics
prompt: Group velocity equals phase velocity when dispersion is?
explain: No dispersion means dv_p/dλ = 0, so group velocity = phase velocity.
